The entry accurately represents the particulate-level descriptions of solids (crystalline and amorphous), liquids, and gases as detailed in Essential Knowledge statements 3.3.A.1 through 3.3.A.4. Topic 3.3, learning objective 3.3.A, requires students to represent differences among solid, liquid, and gas phases using a particulate-level model. The items match 3.3.A.1–3.3.A.4: solids may be crystalline or amorphous and their particles do not undergo overall translation relative to one another; liquid particles are in close contact and continually moving and colliding; and gas particles are in constant motion, with neither a definite volume nor a definite shape. a_factual: Each item matches the CED. Close contact for solids comes from 3.3.A.3 ('the constituent particles are in close contact at all times'). Liquid: 3.3.A.2 says liquid particles are 'in close contact,' 'continually moving and colliding,' and that arrangement and movement are influenced by the nature and strength of forces. 3.3.A.3 supports 'similar molar volume' to the solid. Gas: 3.3.A.4 says particles are in constant motion with 'minimal effects of forces between particles,' collision frequency and spacing depend on temperature, pressure and volume, and the gas has 'neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.'
